summary: The article provides a generally reliable overview of ITR-3 and ITR-4 for AY 2026-27, including eligibility, key schedules, and verification steps, but contains a few inaccuracies regarding specific limits and eligibility conditions for ITR-4.

claims.claim: ITR-4 (Sugam) is for individuals, HUFs, and firms opting for presumptive taxation under Sections 44AD, 44ADA, or 44AE.
claims.note: ITR-4 is indeed for Resident Individuals, HUFs, and Firms (other than LLPs) opting for presumptive taxation under these sections.

claims.claim: For Section 44AD, income is generally declared at 6% of digital receipts and 8% of cash receipts.
claims.note: Under Section 44AD, presumptive income is 6% for digital receipts and 8% for cash receipts.

claims.claim: For Section 44ADA, it's 50% of gross professional receipts.
claims.note: Under Section 44ADA, 50% of gross professional receipts is considered presumptive income.

claims.claim: You can file ITR-4 if you are an individual, HUF, or a partnership firm (excluding LLP) and have: Income from business where turnover does not exceed ₹2 crores and you opt for presumptive taxation under Section 44AD.
claims.note: The turnover limit for Section 44AD is generally ₹2 crores, but can be ₹3 crores if cash receipts do not exceed 5% of the total turnover.

claims.claim: You can file ITR-4 if you are an individual, HUF, or a partnership firm (excluding LLP) and have: Income from profession where gross receipts do not exceed ₹50 lakhs and you opt for presumptive taxation under Section 44ADA.
claims.note: The gross receipts limit for Section 44ADA is ₹50 lakhs, but can be ₹75 lakhs if cash receipts do not exceed 5% of the total gross receipts.

claims.claim: You can file ITR-4 if you are an individual, HUF, or a partnership firm (excluding LLP) and have: Income from plying, hiring, or leasing goods carriages, and you opt for presumptive taxation under Section 44AE.
claims.note: ITR-4 can be filed by individuals, HUFs, and firms (excluding LLPs) opting for presumptive taxation under Section 44AE, provided they do not own more than 10 goods carriages.

claims.claim: However, you cannot file ITR-4 if you have: Income from more than one house property (for AY 2026-27, you can report income from up to two house properties).
claims.note: For AY 2026-27, ITR-4 allows reporting income from up to two house properties.

claims.claim: What is the deadline for filing ITR for individuals with business income? For individuals and HUFs whose accounts are not required to be audited, the deadline for filing ITR-3 and ITR-4 for AY 2026-27 (FY 2025-26) is 31st August 2026.
claims.note: The deadline for filing ITR-3 and ITR-4 for AY 2026-27 (non-audit cases) is August 31, 2026.
